head: The matchup inside the matchup
paras: The Devils (8-5-0) lost 5-2 to Colorado on Wednesday, while the Golden Knights (9-4-1) beat Ottawa 4-1 on Tuesday. Going in, the Devils are third in the Metropolitan and the Knights second in the Pacific.

The Devils keep things calm after the whistle, throw more pucks at the net than almost anyone (32.7 shots a game, second most) and get pinned in their own end on long shifts. Only two teams get pinned in their own end more often. The Golden Knights draw more power plays than they give up, have the league’s best penalty kill and block a lot of shots, and they’re first in discipline and third in blocking shots. So the Devils’ power play against the Golden Knights’ kill is strength against strength. On top of that, the Golden Knights’ defensemen shoot a lot, and the Devils’ not so much.

Jack Hughes leads the Devils with four goals and 14 points, and Nico Hischier has a team-high seven goals. The Golden Knights’ scoring runs through Jack Eichel, who has seven goals and 20 points, and Mark Stone has a team-high eight goals.
Connor Hellebuyck is expected to start for New Jersey (1-0-0, .944 in one start), and Adin Hill for Vegas (5-1-0, .895 in six starts).

items.text: The Golden Knights are newly without Carter Hart. Adin Hill is expected to start.
Brayden McNabb is set to play his 900th NHL game.
Mitch Marner has a point in eight straight games.
The Devils have played better than their record (.615): their chances are worth about .747, and their goaltending has held them back.

VGK.head: Leaning the Golden Knights’ way
VGK.body: The two have been about even at out-chancing opponents lately. Vegas has home-ice advantage. The Devils can still swing it if they keep the shots coming.

NJD.head: Close, but the Golden Knights have the slight edge
NJD.body: The two have been about even at out-chancing opponents lately. Vegas has home-ice advantage. The Devils can tip it if they keep the shots coming.

calls.head: The matchup inside the matchup
calls.body: The Devils are one of the league’s best for the power play, but the Golden Knights are the best at the penalty kill. Our lean: the Devils’ power play wins out. Power plays usually beat kills in these spots.

calls.head: Something has to give
calls.body: The Devils are one of the league’s best for shot volume, but the Golden Knights are near the top at keeping shots away. We’ll side with the Devils.

calls.head: Active D vs. Forward-led
calls.body: On shots from defensemen, Vegas is one of the league’s best, but New Jersey is near the bottom. Watch the Golden Knights’ defensemen jump into the play.
